column9: 4 scenarios x 8 flood reps. FLOOR UNCHANGED at 123; pass_after 165 -> 224 is a REP-COUNT change, not a coverage claim: the flood scenario is now drawn over FLOOD_MERGE_REPS = 8 storms instead of 3, because the app-merge property moved from a per-storm assertion to a SET property over the drawn storms (see tests/it/resize_flood_test.odin). Measured by the orchestrator on the merged tree, result/bin/herdr-session: full it suite 291 pass / 0 fail; gate row resize = 224 against floor 123. THE INVARIANT WAS RE-BASED TWICE, both times because the old form measured the wrong thing: (1) the denominator moved from `resizes` (SIGWINCH delivered AND counted by the app — the kernel coalesces before that counter runs, so it is scheduler luck) to `issued` (the resize requests the harness itself made: deterministic, ours). Headline: passes*2 <= issued. (2) APP-MERGED `passes < resizes` was DROPPED as a per-storm check and replaced by the set-level `max_run >= 2` requirement, because when the kernel spaces deliveries out the app has no merge opportunity at all — observed resizes=8 passes=8 max_run=1 on an IDLE box, 1 failure in 3 runs, and 4/90 under load. Reps that never reached the counters are measured=false, NOT counted as max_run=0, so an unmeasured storm cannot quietly pad the aggregate. WHY THE SET CHECK IS NOT REDUNDANT — measured on a merge-disabled mutant: the headline alone LEAKS. In ~4 of 8 storms per run, `passes*2 <= issued` went green on an app that merged nothing (issued=30 resizes=11 passes=11, and 12/12, 14/14, 15/15 — all <= 30), and passes <= resizes holds with equality. Only the set-level max_run >= 2 closes it: 10 runs out of 10 red on the mutant. The check is not vacuous either: 318/320 storms showed max_run >= 2, and only 2 storms in 320 had max_run == 1 (exactly the no-opportunity cases that broke the old per-rep check). KNOWN REMAINING FLAKE, NOT THIS ROW'S PRODUCT: `the surviving frame is the FINAL size` fails ~2% of storms (7/320 measured here, 3/120 on the pre-change binary — pre-existing, rate unchanged). Root cause is the pty SCREEN EMULATOR, not the app: screen_resize -> screen_init zeroes carry_len (tests/pty/screen.odin:98), dropping a UTF-8 sequence in flight across the resize boundary; its continuation bytes decode as U+FFFD, rh_is_rule then fails on the mojibake and the rule count drops 2 -> 1 at a CORRECT width. The app was exonerated directly: in real failing reps the driver's raw stream had 0 orphan continuation bytes. Fix belongs in tests/pty/screen.odin (preserve `carry` across screen_resize) — dispatched separately, tracked in .pi/plans/2026-10-20-odin-test-migration/KNOWN-DEFECT-screen-resize-carry.md.

Independent re-verification by the orchestrator after merge: pty tier 67 / 27 / 163 / 52 all PASS, and 8 fresh resize_flood runs = 64 storms with 0 frame-check failures and 0 failures of any kind (was ~1-2%). NOTE ON INVOCATION: the pty binary must be built with -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1 -- without it two pre-existing tests fail (driver_timing_requires_a_single_threaded_runner and an fd-leak check). A sibling defect found while fixing that one is ALSO NOW FIXED (commit 97d63b4, +55 assertions, same screen_test group, so this row carries both). That defect: a resize landing mid-ESCAPE / mid-CSI / mid-OSC reset the parser, so CONTROL BYTES PAINTED AS VISIBLE TEXT -- mid-OSC leaked the window title onto the grid (row0='tle:secretcd'), mid-CSI left '3HAGAIN', mid-`ESC (` re-created the exact charset smear this emulator exists to prevent. Worse than the carry bug because it manufactures content that was never drawn. DESIGN: preserve parser state (option a), NOT void-and-swallow -- a real terminal's parser lives in the input layer and SIGWINCH never touches it, so the sequence completes against the NEW geometry. Voiding was rejected on a concrete failure mode: it drops a positioning verb the app really sent, leaving the cursor where it was while the app believes it moved, corrupting the NEXT frame instead of this one -- invisible to the very no-literal-escape-bytes check that voiding exists to satisfy. SIDE FIX INSIDE THE SAME FILE (slightly beyond the literal brief, reported by the lane): the COLUMN out-of-bounds CUP path was silently discarding glyphs while the ROW path counted them; screen_put_cursor now counts it too, so an out-of-range cursor lands as dropped+=, never as silent loss. `dropped` itself now survives resize (it is a stream-level audit -- wiping it deletes the evidence the counter exists to provide; nothing else in the repo reads it). column1: # WHY `pty` IS ITS OWN TIER AND NOT `hermetic`
# Verified (D-T15): a real pty WORKS in the nix sandbox -- /dev/ptmx is
# present and a child can take a controlling terminal. So this tier belongs in
# `nix flake check` and does NOT need the armed remote fixture.
# It is still not the hermetic tier. It requires a device node hermetic tests
# must never depend on, and a sandbox built without /dev/ptmx has to be able to
# exclude these four rows WITHOUT taking the whole hermetic suite down. Folding
# them into `hermetic` would couple them: one missing device node, and every
# hermetic row fails for a reason that has nothing to do with what it tests.
# THE GATE NO LONGER DEFAULTS AN UNKNOWN TIER TO HERMETIC. It refuses the row
# out loud. Until this change, a typo in the tier column -- or a new tier the
# gate had not been taught, exactly like `pty` before now -- was silently filed
# under hermetic. With tiering load-bearing for T15 that is the worst possible
# failure: the tier column would look authoritative while being a guess.
# VERIFIED BY SCRIPT, NOT BY HAND:  bash tests/tools/hscheck/check_parity_arith.sh
# That script re-reads these rows and reconciles them against their origin. If you
# change a floor, it will fail until you update the origin list in the SAME commit.
# The comment below is a rendering of what the script computes; the script is the
# authority. Hand-maintained totals in a file that changes every time a lane lands
# are not verification, they are a claim that goes stale quietly.
